stakeholders.name: European Commission / CSRD Regulators
stakeholders.description: The CSRD (Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive) requires large EU-listed FMCG companies to report against all 12 ESRS standards from 2025. Non-compliance carries substantial fines and potential market access restrictions.

engagement_tactics.option: Implement ESRS E1-E5 (environmental) and S1-S4 (social) reporting systems
engagement_tactics.rationale: Achieves full CSRD compliance and avoids enforcement actions

engagement_tactics.option: Report minimum required standards and exclude voluntary disclosures
engagement_tactics.rationale: Compliant but signals low ESG ambition to EU market

stakeholders.name: European Conscious Consumers
stakeholders.description: 66% of European consumers say they actively avoid brands linked to environmental or social harm (Edelman Trust Barometer 2024). The EU Green Claims Directive will make unsubstantiated sustainability claims illegal from 2026.

engagement_tactics.option: Obtain third-party verified eco-labels (EU Ecolabel, Rainforest Alliance)
Use generic green messaging without certification
engagement_tactics.rationale: Risks EU Green Claims Directive enforcement from 2026

stakeholders.name: Tier-2 Agricultural Suppliers
stakeholders.description: The EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) requires FMCG companies to conduct human rights and environmental due diligence across their entire value chain, including tier-2 and tier-3 suppliers in origin countries.

engagement_tactics.option: Extend supplier code of conduct to tier-2 and conduct on-site audits
engagement_tactics.rationale: Required by CSDDD; reduces supply chain liability

engagement_tactics.option: Limit due diligence to tier-1 direct suppliers only
engagement_tactics.rationale: Insufficient under CSDDD; creates legal and reputational exposure

stakeholders.name: Major Retail Buyers (Carrefour, Tesco, Lidl)
stakeholders.description: European supermarket chains increasingly impose supplier ESG scorecards, plastic reduction targets, and Scope 3 emission requirements as listing conditions. Failure to meet buyer standards results in delisting.

engagement_tactics.option: Join the Consumer Goods Forum and commit to deforestation-free sourcing
engagement_tactics.rationale: Meets the primary buyer-coalition ESG benchmark

engagement_tactics.option: Negotiate ESG requirements down in commercial contracts
engagement_tactics.rationale: Short-term savings risk delisting as standards tighten

stakeholders.name: EU Packaging & Plastics Regulators
stakeholders.description: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR, 2024) mandates recycled content minimums, reusability targets, and extended producer responsibility schemes. Non-compliance triggers import bans on non-compliant packaging.

engagement_tactics.option: Transition to fully recyclable or reusable packaging across all SKUs by 2027
engagement_tactics.rationale: Gets ahead of the PPWR compliance curve

engagement_tactics.option: Apply for PPWR derogations on cost grounds
engagement_tactics.rationale: Buys time but does not solve structural compliance gap
